description: Read events and the internal revision before editing. Request include_facets first and select returned values for known labels. Facet results describe the entire published active feed, independent of read filters or pagination. Nonempty filters also return filtered_subscription with canonical filters, matching_event_count and unmatched_filter_values. Use its URLs for that selection; top-level subscription URLs remain unfiltered. Event IDs, external keys, dates, removal state and pagination narrow only the read, never the subscription. Filtering changes no events and creates no cloned feed. Before proposing cancellations from a revised PDF/document, read every page of the unfiltered feed; never infer deletion from omitted events. These tools manage Smart Calendars feeds only; they cannot access mailboxes or start source monitoring, scheduled PDF checks or document refreshes. For requests solely for those unsupported actions, explain the limitation without reading feeds or substituting an edit. For unsupported mailbox requests, offer to work with schedule content the user chooses to provide instead. General ICS explanations need no account access. When sharing a feed or filtered_subscription with distribution_ready=true, offer "Open in calendar app" using that object’s HTTPS subscription_open_url (it redirects to webcal), and "Calendar options" using its subscription_options_url for Apple/default, Google, Outlook and copy-link choices. Retain subscription_url as a copyable HTTPS fallback. Prefer these HTTPS handoff links over putting subscription_webcal_url directly in chat, because some clients do not preserve clickable webcal links. If a handoff URL is absent, use the HTTPS subscription_url and dashboard subscription controls instead. Offer "View or edit" using the feed’s manage_url. For a filtered selection use the nested filtered_subscription links, not the unfiltered feed links. Use the returned URLs exactly; never invent or rewrite their host, path or token. Opening a link does not confirm a subscription; the user must confirm in their calendar app. Do not present inactive or unpublished feeds as ready to subscribe. When returning a filtered subscription, explain: filters select events, not who can access them; anyone with the link can remove the filters and read the full published calendar.

filters.description: Request include_facets first; use returned available_facets values for the desired known labels. Values are trimmed and case-insensitive; format accepts attendance-mode aliases. Values within a field use OR; different fields use AND. Unknown values never broaden the selection. Filtering cannot infer missing metadata.

city.description: An existing event-city facet selected from available_facets.city. Not the user’s current city or residence; never request user geolocation.

country.description: An existing event-country facet selected from available_facets.country. Not the user’s nationality or residence; never request user geolocation.

person.description: An event participant or organizer from available_facets.person, not an account or profile lookup.

source.description: Child-feed/source identifier from available_facets.source, not a source URL.

venue.description: An event venue selected from available_facets.venue, not a user-location lookup.

include_facets.description: Return available_facets ({value,label,count} entries), facet_coverage ({tagged_events,fallback_events,missing_events}), facets_truncated and facet_scope=published_active_events. Coverage distinguishes explicit tags, fallbacks and missing values; title/location fallbacks do not infer classifications or audiences. Also returned for nonempty filters. Canonical fields: person, venue, topic, city, country, format, source.
